title: Clinical study on radiation dose reduction in patients with cervical lymph node metastatic HPV (human papilloma virus)-positive squamous cell carcinoma of the oropharynx based on tumor tissue oxygenation as detected by 18F-fluoro-misonidazole positron emission tomography (18F-FMISO-PET)
summary: In this feasibility study, the effectiveness of dose reduction of postoperative radiotherapy in patients with malignant tumors of the tonsils, soft palate or base of tongue is going to be investigated.
conditions: Patients with HPV-positive T1-2, N1.2c, M0 oropharyngeal (tonsils, soft palate, base of tongue) carcinoma; Patients with HPV-positive Tx N1-2c, M0 cervical CUP syndrome (Cancer of Unknown Primary)

interventions.name: Patients with HPV-positive T1-2, N1-2c, M0 oropharyngeal carcinoma or patients with HPV-positive Tx N1-2c, M0 cervical CUP syndrome (Cancer of Unknown Primary) who show good oxygenation in 18F-FMISO-PET are going to be treated postoperatively with adjuvant radiotherapy with a reduced radiation dose

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with HPV-positive T1-2, N1-2c, M0 oropharyngeal carcinoma
- Patients with HPV-positive Tx N1-2c, M0 cervical CUP syndrome (Cancer of Unknown Primary)
- Age: ≥ 18 years
- With or without resection of the primary tumor mentioned above and indication for radiotherapy
- Written informed consent of the study participants after written and oral verbal informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Any previous radiotherapy in the head and neck area
- Previous chemotherapy in the context of newly diagnosed 
   oropharyngeal carcinoma
- Previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy within the last three years
- Distant metastasis
- Patients with histologically HPV-negative squamous cell carcinoma (PLECAs)
- T-stage greater than T2 (i.e. patients with T3 or T4 oropharyngeal PLECAs are 
   excluded) 
- Age < 18 years 
- Patients for whom MR (magnetic resonance imaging) imaging is contraindicated (e.g. in the presence of implants not suitable for MR)
